results.name: Brachiosaurus Skull #RealityScan
results.description:
Museum für Naturkunde Berlin

> The Brachiosaurus skull shown here is based on a three-dimensional digital scanning of the original, making it absolutely identical to the fossil. The very, large mires under the thin arch of bone is striking. The actual nostrils of the living animal were at the front of the snout and not on top of the skull as was often assumed previously. The large hollow behind them probably functioned as a resonating chamber to produce sound. 

[More info](https://www.museumfuernaturkunde.berlin/de/museum/ausstellungen/saurierwelt).

96 images, Google Pixel 6a

results.name: Simple Stegosaurus Skeleton
results.description:
Stegosaurus (/ˌstɛɡəˈsɔːrəs/), from Greek stegos (στέγος) which means roof and sauros (σαῦρος) which means lizard (Greek: Στεγόσαυρος), is a genus of herbivorous thyreophoran dinosaur. Fossils of this genus date to the Late Jurassic period, where they are found in Kimmeridgian to early Tithonian aged strata, between 155 and 150 million years ago, in the western United States and Portugal. Of the species that have been classified in the upper Morrison Formation of the western US, only three are universally recognized; S. stenops, S. ungulatus and S. sulcatus. The remains of over 80 individual animals of this genus have been found. Stegosaurus would have lived alongside dinosaurs such as Apatosaurus, Diplodocus, Brachiosaurus, Allosaurus, and Ceratosaurus; the latter two may have been predators of it.

Info Link: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stegosaurus

results.name: Brachiosaurus
results.description: Brachiosaurus (/ˌbrækiəˈsɔːrəs/) is a genus of sauropod dinosaur that lived in North America during the Late Jurassic, about 154 to 150 million years ago.[1] It was first described by American paleontologist Elmer S. Riggs in 1903 from fossils found in the Colorado River valley in western Colorado, United States. Riggs named the dinosaur Brachiosaurus altithorax; the generic name is Greek for "arm lizard", in reference to its proportionately long arms, and the specific name means "deep chest". Brachiosaurus is estimated to have been between 18 and 22 meters (59 and 72 ft) long; body mass estimates of the subadult holotype specimen range from 28.3 to 46.9 metric tons (31.2 and 51.7 short tons). It had a disproportionately long neck, small skull, and large overall size, all of which are typical for sauropods. Atypically, Brachiosaurus had longer forelimbs than hindlimbs, which resulted in a steeply inclined trunk, and a proportionally shorter tail.

results.name: Animated Argentinosaurus (Free)
results.description: This is a 3D model of an Argentinosaurus, one of the largest sauropod dinosaurs ever. The model is ultra-realistic with accurate proportions, detailed skin textures, and anatomically correct features. It is sculpted in Blender using advanced techniques, featuring quad topology and PBR materials. Despite its high level of detail and professional quality, this model is completely free to download. Perfect for educational purposes, personal projects, or as a reference for paleoart enthusiasts.

results.name: Brachiosaurus V1
results.description:
This brachiosaurus model represents my first major effort to do high-end sculpting and texturing. I also optimized its rig to make it as animation-friendly as I could. 
Unfortunately, Blender cannot pack UDIM textures at this point, so I opted to leave all the textures off, but everything is UV unwrapped and ready for you to texture! 
Just make sure to credit me in any project you use this asset in! Enjoy!
